deal_context: Test session: Buyer reviewing Seller-form PSA for commercial property acquisition in Washington state.

risk_inventory.title: Uncapped Buyer Indemnification for Inspections
risk_inventory.description: Buyer's indemnification of Seller for inspection-related costs, expenses, damages, and liabilities is uncapped and survives termination. This creates open-ended liability exposure for Buyer with no time or dollar limitation.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: Buyer shall indemnify and hold Seller harmless from and against all costs, expenses, damages, liabilities

amplified_by.effect: Survival provision ensures this indemnity outlasts the agreement

risk_inventory.title: Knowledge Qualifier Limited to Actual Knowledge
risk_inventory.description: Seller's knowledge is defined as the 'actual knowledge' of a single individual with no duty of inquiry or investigation. This allows Seller to disclaim knowledge of material defects that a reasonable investigation would reveal.

amplified_by.effect: All substantive seller reps are qualified by this narrow knowledge standard

risk_inventory.title: Broad AS-IS Waiver of Implied Warranties
risk_inventory.description: Buyer accepts the property entirely AS-IS with no representations or warranties beyond those expressly stated. Combined with the narrow knowledge qualifier, this significantly limits Buyer's post-closing remedies for property defects.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: BUYER ACKNOWLEDGES AND AGREES THAT, EXCEPT FOR SELLER’S EXPRESS REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

mitigated_by.effect: Express representations provide limited carve-outs from AS-IS

amplified_by.effect: Release provision further limits post-closing recourse

risk_inventory.title: Broad Release of Seller Claims Upon Deed Acceptance
risk_inventory.description: By accepting the deed, Buyer releases Seller from virtually all claims related to the property. While there is a carve-out for express representations, the breadth of the release substantially limits Buyer's post-closing remedies.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: By accepting the Deed to the Property, Buyer, on behalf of itself, its officers, directors

mitigated_by.effect: Carve-out preserves claims under express representations

amplified_by.effect: AS-IS clause compounds the release by eliminating implied warranty claims

risk_inventory.title: Short Survival Period for Representations
risk_inventory.description: Seller's representations and warranties survive closing for a limited period. If defects are discovered after the survival period expires, Buyer has no contractual recourse regardless of the defect's nature or severity.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: Any cause of action of a party for a breach of the representations and warranties

amplified_by.effect: Narrow knowledge qualifier means fewer discoverable breaches within the survival window

risk_inventory.title: Title Review Period May Be Insufficient
risk_inventory.description: Buyer has only ten (10) days from the Effective Date to review title. For complex commercial properties with multiple encumbrances, easements, or CC&Rs, this may not provide adequate time for thorough title analysis.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: Buyer shall have ten (10) days from the Effective Date

mitigated_by.effect: Seller must deliver title documents within seven days, giving partial overlap

risk_inventory.title: Ordinary Course Covenant Limited to Due Diligence Period
risk_inventory.description: Seller's covenant to maintain and operate the property in the ordinary course applies only during the Due Diligence Period, not through Closing. This creates a gap period where Seller has reduced obligations regarding property management.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: During the Due Diligence Period, Seller shall continue to maintain, operate, and lease the Property

amplified_by.effect: Service contract restrictions also have limited temporal scope

risk_inventory.title: Earnest Money Deposit at Risk Before Due Diligence Complete
risk_inventory.description: Buyer must deliver the initial deposit within business days of the Effective Date, before completing due diligence. If Buyer fails to timely approve due diligence, the deposit refund mechanism and any conditions should be clearly defined.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: Within ______ (__) business day(s) after the Effective Date, Buyer shall deliver

mitigated_by.effect: Due diligence contingency provides a refund path if Buyer disapproves

amplified_by.effect: Additional deposit further increases exposure before closing

risk_inventory.title: Conditions Precedent May Be Waived by Conduct
risk_inventory.description: The waiver provision for conditions precedent should be reviewed to ensure conditions cannot be inadvertently waived by conduct or silence, which could force a party to close without all contractual protections being satisfied.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: The conditions set forth in Sections 5.1 through 5.4

risk_inventory.title: Litigation Representation Qualified by Knowledge
risk_inventory.description: Seller's representation regarding pending or threatened litigation is qualified by Seller's Actual Knowledge. Litigation is a factual matter that should not require a knowledge qualifier — Seller either has or has not been served with process.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: To Seller’s Actual Knowledge, there is no litigation pending or threatened against Seller

amplified_by.effect: Narrow knowledge definition compounds the weakness of this representation

risk_inventory.title: Opportunity: Require Buyer Consent for All Contract Modifications
risk_inventory.description: Seller is prohibited from entering into, materially modifying, or terminating service contracts. However, the 'materiality' qualifier leaves room for minor modifications that could cumulatively impact the property's operation. Consider requiring Buyer consent for all modifications, not just material ones.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: Seller shall not enter into, materially modify or terminate any Service Contracts

risk_inventory.title: Post-Closing Knowledge Limitation Reduces Buyer Remedies
risk_inventory.description: If Buyer learns of a breach of Seller's representations before closing and proceeds anyway, Buyer may be deemed to have waived the breach. This creates a perverse incentive for Buyer not to investigate too thoroughly before closing.
risk_inventory.highlight_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement to the contrary, in the event the Closing occurs

amplified_by.effect: Short survival period further limits window for discovering and asserting breaches

inspection_rights.value: Buyer access with insurance and indemnification requirements

approval_mechanism.value: Buyer may approve or disapprove in sole discretion

title_standard.value: Fee simple via Special Warranty Deed

seller_reps_scope.value: Authority, rent roll, compliance, litigation, condemnation, leases

knowledge_standard.value: Actual knowledge of designated individual only

as_is_provision.value: Buyer accepts property AS-IS except for express representations

release_scope.value: Broad release upon deed acceptance with rep carve-out

operations.value: Maintain in ordinary course during DD period

insurance.value: Maintain existing casualty and liability insurance
